pass_b_english: “I will confess to you, Lord, with my whole heart; I will recount all your wonders” (Psalm 9:1).

But others say the present psalm is sung to him, not about him, the prophet confessing on behalf of human nature, saying that it is proper to the perfect to dedicate the whole heart to God: “For you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart,” etc. (Deuteronomy 6:5).

And what “with my whole heart” now indicates, and what he does: having foreseen the things to come with prophetic eyes, he recounts them, making the hearers partners of the confession, having as joy the fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22), and recounting the wonders of God with lifted-up contemplations.

choices.why: The psalm is sung as address to God, not as speech about him. CF inverted the pair.
rejected: concerning him rather than to him

choices.why: Dedicating the whole heart is the mark of the τέλειοι. Not ‘the prophet’s perfect nature’.
OCR ο λῃ is ὅλῃ. Not an uncertain corruption.
